methodologyNote: Historical feed built from real primary sources, not a synthetic model: the August 1933 Manchester Corporation Transport Guide (41 day tram routes and about 60 bus routes) merged with the December 1938 County Borough of Stockport Bus & Tram Time Tables (11 tram routes and 22 bus routes). Stockport's 11 tram routes are included, and their Manchester to Stockport and Hazel Grove trunk keeps its real transcribed point-to-point times. Bus routes are full point-to-point clock timetables, used verbatim. MCT's own April 1943 wartime guide (trams, buses and trolleybuses) is offered as a second era; it is a heavily pruned wartime remnant, so 1933, the network near its peak, is the representative vintage. No running-time table survives for either MCT book's trams, so their times come from a track-based model, the method used for Birmingham. Every route over a stretch of track gets the same time. Cars keep to 12 mph on inner streets (within a mile of Piccadilly Gardens and 700 m of each borough centre) and a fitted 15.7 mph elsewhere, calling at stops every 300 m with realistic acceleration, braking and a 12 s dwell. The model is fitted to Manchester's own real tram times (the Stockport 1938 trunk routes, and Middleton to Manchester, 29 min in 1930), with a leave-one-out error of 1.6 min. Checked out of sample, it runs about 8% fast against Birmingham's official 1930s route times and 11% fast against Liverpool's 1937 guide, mostly on short inner routes, so 1930s times near the centre may still be a little optimistic. Salford is included in both eras as partial historical data: ten transcribed MCT routes serve it, but Salford Corporation's own tram timetables were not found, so 1933 figures there are a lower bound (an upper-bound scenario runs Salford Corporation's surveyed track at the median printed MCT headway). Bus routes follow real roads. Transfer penalty 5 min per change (the low end of published interchange valuations, about 5-18 min). A trams-only / buses-only / combined mode toggle is available. Routing is inbound (arrive by target) for both eras, the same convention as Liverpool and Sheffield. No coastline clipping.

robustness.basis: trams 11% slower (the tram model's out-of-sample bias against Liverpool's printed times); best case adds Salford Corporation trams on the surveyed track at the median printed MCT headway (their own timetables were not found)
trams 11% slower; buses timed from derived speeds 15% slower or faster
